questions.worked_solution:
To evaluate ${160}^{2},$ we start by writing it out with a multiplication sign:

$$
{160}^{2}={{160\times 160}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ times}}
$$

Then, we work out $160\times 160.$

First, we figure out the non-zero part and the block of zeros for both numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned}160 & \,⟶\,160 \\ 160 & \,⟶\,160\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that there are $2$ zeros in total.

Next, we multiply the non-zero parts:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{} \\ \boxed{3}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\,\end{aligned} & \,\, & \begin{aligned}\end{aligned} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we join the above with the block of zeros: 

$$
25600=25,600
$$

Therefore, ${160}^{2}=25,600.$

{700}^{2}={{700\times 700}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ times}}
$$

Then, we work out $700\times 700.$

First, we figure out the non-zero part and the block of zeros for both numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned}700 & \,⟶\,700 \\ 700 & \,⟶\,700\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that there are $4$ zeros in total.

Next, we multiply the non-zero parts:

$$
7\times 7=49
$$

Finally, we join the above with the block of zeros: 

$$
490000=490,000
$$

Therefore, ${700}^{2}=490,000.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To evaluate $220^2,$ we start by writing it out with a multiplication sign:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131634/assets/e963c6c194b0cf3991be02d43f130eb81cd3e6f16b1b6921718468b3752ddc07.svg)

Then, we work out $220 \times 220.$

First, we figure out the non-zero part and the block of zeros for both numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned}220 & \,⟶\,220 \\ 220 & \,⟶\,220\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that there are $2$ zeros in total.

Next, we multiply the non-zero parts:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  &  & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\,\end{aligned} & \,\, & \begin{aligned}\end{aligned} \\  & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we join the above with the block of zeros: 

$$
{\color{red}484}{\color{blue}00}= 48,400
$$

Therefore, $220^2  =   48,400.$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
To evaluate a large exponent, we first write out the power using multiplication signs as usual. Then, we calculate the product by splitting it into groups of two-digit multiplications, before calculating the resulting product. 

For example, let's evaluate $2^4.$

First, we write
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131634/assets/4ccd929bbf46272fe64264465ed639c841643ec0e6c42d053d66555faa910dff.svg)

Since $2 \times 2 = 4,$ we have

$$
\underbrace{2 \times 2}_{\large \color{blue}4} \times \underbrace{2 \times 2}_{\large \color{blue}4} = {\color{blue}4} \times {\color{blue}4}.
$$

Finally, we work out $4\times 4.$
Since $4\times 4=16,$ we conclude that 

$$
2^4=16.
$$
